mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding future equity present value.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-year moving average and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the pre-tightening average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength and impending market volatility, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% month-over-month while INDPRO falls by >1% month-over-month for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market softening
failure_condition: Over 100 instances where the above pattern occurs, the 20-day forward return is non-negative in >70% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) exceeding 5% year-over-year, when consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) is below 3%, predicts a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals resilient demand without price pressure.
candidate_trigger: HOUST YoY growth > 5% and CPIAUCSL < 100 for the current month
failure_condition: Across 500 matched triggers, the 60-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A double-dip decline in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a rebound above the prior low, when accompanied by a decline in consumer confidence (unavailable proxy, so omitted), predicts a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates supply-side normalization.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months then rises by >3% in the third month
failure_condition: In 100 such recovery windows, the 5-day forward return is negative in more than 50% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of declining unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% for three consecutive months coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate continued accommodative policy.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains below 4% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: During 200 such episodes, the 20-day forward return is not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 100,000 jobs, followed by a decline in manufacturing activity (not available), would typically be paired with a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return due to over-heating labor markets and risk-off flows.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >100,000 in a single month
failure_condition: Across 50 such spikes, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 80% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales proxy (not available) and a sustained rise in consumer spending (not available) would typically be modeled as a missing variable interaction, but here we proxy with a combined signal: a 2-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a 3-month rise in home sales (HOUST) predicts a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as demand recovers.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months then HOUST rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 200 matched recovery patterns, the 20-day forward return is not positive in more than 70% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) followed by a sustained decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two months predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals persistent supply-side stress and deflationary risk.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% month-over-month for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 200 for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Persistent supply shock and deflationary cycle
failure_condition: During 150 matched episodes, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% of cases (binomial test p < 0.05).
